chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man from whose urethra something comes out after he has performed ghusl. He said: He must perform ghusl and repeat the salat, unless he had urinated before performing ghusl; then he does not repeat his ghusl.

Muhammad said: And Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: Whoever performs ghusl while in janabah before urinating, then later finds moisture, his ghusl has been invalidated. But if he had urinated and then performed ghusl, then later found moisture, his ghusl is not invalidated; rather, wudu (ablution) is required of him.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer) that must be repeated in this case
key_terms.بَلَلًا: moisture or wetness found after ghusl
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in the state of janabah

ai.seo_question: Does moisture discharged after ghusl from janabah invalidate the ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling concerning moisture exiting after ghusl from janabah. If a person did not urinate before ghusl and later finds moisture, the ghusl is invalidated; but if he urinated before ghusl, the ghusl remains valid and only wudu (ablution) is required.
